10	## 1. Goal
11

130	disclosed only in their own commit messages: `zimmSizeChip.css.test.ts`, `zimmSizeChipGroup.css.test.ts`,
131	`zimmSlideIndicator.css.test.ts` (dedicated recipe unit tests, beyond the four-file template above), and
132	`organisms/zimmProductCard/nodeCoverage/index.stories.tsx` (a per-Figma-node coverage folder). None cross a

134	`ui-kits/`.

136	---
137	
138	## 4. Architecture decisions
139	
140	**Variation axis = discriminated union (data contract) + declarative config table (layout).**
141	`typescript.md` mandates the union, and the ACs require it: Wishlist alone needs `colour` + `size` + mandatory
142	`onRemove`; PLP alone needs `sizes` + `onNotifyMe`. A flat optional-everything bag lets you build a Wishlist
143	card with no remove CTA (AC violation) and a PLP card with one (design violation).
144	
145	```
146	ZimmProductCardProps = Base & (PlpVariation | HomeVariation | WishlistVariation)
147	  base:       id, href, name, headingLevel, primaryImage, hoverImage?, images?,
148	              currentPrice?, originalPrice?, isUnavailable?, badge?
149	  'plp':      sizes?, selectedSize?, onSizeSelect?, onAddToBag?, onNotifyMe?
150	  'home':     —
151	  'wishlist': colour, size, onRemove (required), onAddToBag?
152	```
153	
154	`'recently-viewed'` is **not** a fourth member — the AC says it behaves identically to PLP, so consumers pass
155	`variation: 'plp'`. Recorded as an assumption, not a silent choice.
156	
157	The render body must **not** `switch` on `props.variation`. Layout comes from a module-level `VARIATION_CONFIG`
158	(`showBag`, `showAttributes`, `showRemove`, `hoverHidesPrice`, `hoverRevealsPrice`, `hoverRevealsSizeSelector`,
159	`hoverSwapsImage`). That is what satisfies the extensibility AC: add a union member + a config row, touch no JSX.
160	
161	**The card is fluid, not 288px.** `gridSystem.ts` has `maxWidth: 'none'`. Figma's 288/179 are widths at the
162	reference artboards. The card fills its grid cell (`width: 100%`); the image holds ratio via `aspectRatio`.
163	Grid placement belongs to SFCC-80.
164	
165	**Mobile/desktop boundary = 768px** (`breakpoints.md`, 48em) — the only confirmed foundation breakpoint between
166	the 402 and 1440 artboards, and where the grid already goes 4→8 columns. `min-width` is inclusive, so the 768
167	artboard gets the desktop card. Every hover rule is additionally gated on `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`
168	so a 768px touch tablet never gets hover-only content. See OQ-5.
169	
170	**Hover is CSS-only, keyed on `:hover, :focus-within`.** No React hover state — 60 tiles re-rendering on pointer
171	move is a PLP perf defect. `:focus-within` is not optional: WCAG 2.2 AA requires the revealed size selector and
172	arrows be keyboard-reachable. All reveal selectors live in one place, the organism's recipe root part, selecting
173	descendants by the shared `data-card-slot` constants. Molecules stay hover-agnostic.
174	
175	**One link per card (stretched-link).** The card holds a bag button, arrows, size options and a remove button —
176	nesting those in an `<a>` is invalid HTML and an a11y failure. The link wraps the product name only and carries
177	a `::after { position:absolute; inset:0 }` overlay; controls get `position:relative; z-index:1`. `href` arrives
178	pre-prefixed from the page. Uses `import {Link as RouteLink} from 'react-router-dom'` per `zimmColourSwatch` —
179	there is no `overrides/app/components/link/` override, contrary to a claim in `overrideStyling.md`.
180	
181	**Reuse, don't rebuild:** `ZimmProductName`, `ZimmProductPrice`, `ZimmIcon` (`bag`, `close`, `chevron-left`,
182	`chevron-right` all exist in `ICON_MAP`). No new icons.
183	
184	**VIC pricing is not a card concern** — precedence is the page mapper's job. Deferred to SFCC-778 (OQ-6).
185	
186	---
187	
188	## 4a. Arrows vs. indicator — RESOLVED (Marcel, 2026-09-02)
189	
190	> *"position indicator is just for tablet and mobile, desktop hover is arrows"*
191	
192	The two are **mutually exclusive**, not paired. Consequences for Steps 1 and 4:
193	
194	**Split by pointer capability, not viewport width.** The gate is
195	`@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` — the same gate every other hover rule already uses:
196	
197	- **hover-capable + fine pointer** → prev/next arrow buttons, revealed on `:hover, :focus-within`. No indicator.
198	- **everything else (touch tablet, mobile)** → `ZimmSlideIndicator`, always visible. No arrows.
199	
200	Capability rather than width is what actually delivers the stated intent: the 768 artboard is a *touch* tablet,
201	and a width rule alone would give it arrows it can never hover to reveal. It also keeps this consistent with the
202	card's own hover rules rather than introducing a second, differently-keyed breakpoint. **Edge case, accepted:**
203	a desktop browser resized below 768 keeps arrows (it still has a fine pointer); a touch-screen laptop gets the
204	indicator. Both are the safe failure direction — nobody is shown a control they cannot operate.
205	
206	**Two knock-on changes to the step pass criteria:**
207	
208	1. **Step 1 — the indicator is NOT `aria-hidden` on touch.** The original criterion assumed the arrow buttons
209	   announce position, so the indicator could be hidden as duplicate. Where the indicator renders there are **no
210	   arrows**, so it becomes the only position signal — hiding it would be a 1.1.1 information loss. It needs an
211	   accessible position announcement (e.g. a visually-hidden "Image 3 of 8" live region, or `role="group"` with
212	   `aria-label`). Revised criterion: exposed and announced when it is the sole affordance.
213	2. **Step 4 — mobile image paging has no mechanism and no AC.** If the indicator shows position on touch, some
214	   touch gesture must change the image. No AC covers this; the ACs only describe desktop hover. See OQ-11.
215	
216	---
217	
218	## 4b. Touch image paging — RESOLVED (Marcel, 2026-09-02)
219	
220	> *"scroll-snap it is"*
221	
222	Native CSS scroll-snap. The dots remain a **passive readout**, visually unchanged from Figma — no enlargement,
223	no conversion to tap targets, so no departure from the design and no WCAG 2.5.8 problem to solve.
224	
225	**Implementation shape: one scroll container on every breakpoint, not two mechanisms.**
226	
227	The image strip is always a horizontally scrollable flex container with `scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'` and
228	`scrollSnapAlign: 'start'` on each slide. What differs by pointer capability is only the *affordance* layered
229	over it:
230	
231	| | Mechanism | Affordance |
232	|---|---|---|
233	| hover + fine pointer | same scroll container | arrows call `scrollBy()`; no indicator |
234	| touch | same scroll container | native drag; indicator reflects position |
235	
236	One container rather than two code paths means a single source of truth for "which image is showing", the
237	arrows become progressive enhancement over something that already works, and the desktop path inherits
238	keyboard scrollability for free.
239	
240	**Active-index derivation:** prefer `IntersectionObserver` on the slides over a scroll listener — 60 tiles on a
241	PLP make a per-scroll-event listener a real perf cost, and the repo already has
242	`overrides/app/hooks/use-intersection-observer.ts` (**Tier 2 — import it, do not modify it**). The `scrollend`
243	event is an acceptable alternative. Left to the Implementer; either satisfies the pass criteria.
244	
245	**Precedent:** the base `ProductScroller`
246	(`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-scroller/index.jsx:79-84`) already uses
247	`scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'` with `overflowX: 'scroll'`. Same technique, already proven in this codebase.
248	
249	**Accepted caveat:** swipe has no explicit affordance beyond the dots implying further content. This is the
250	universal mobile convention, and the alternative (enlarging 1px dots into 24×24 tap targets) trades an
251	invisible-but-expected gesture for a visible-but-off-design control. **Action: flag to Kiera that the mobile
252	gesture is undocumented in the design**, so it lands in the spec rather than being discovered in QA.
253	
254	**Added Step 4 pass criteria:**
255	- The slide container carries `scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'`; every slide carries `scrollSnapAlign`.
256	- Arrows are rendered only under `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`; the indicator only outside it; assert the
257	  two never coexist in the same DOM.
258	- Arrow activation moves the scroll position (assert `scrollBy`/`scrollTo` is called — jsdom does not lay out,
259	  so assert the call, not the resulting offset).
260	- The indicator's active index tracks the observed slide, and clamps at both ends.
261	- A single-image product renders no indicator, no arrows, and no horizontal overflow.
262	- No gesture library is added — `package.json` is untouched (AGENTS.md Hard Rule #7).
263	
264	---
265	
266	## 4c. Badge — RESOLVED (Marcel, 2026-09-02), and it corrects the decomposition
267	
268	Nine nodes supplied; all resolve off one parent, `40001471:20702` "Badge" (a documentation board).
269	`40001471:20682` is its cover slide, not a component.
270	
271	**There are TWO badge components, not one:**
272	
273	| Component set | Node | Variants | Size |
274	|---|---|---|---|
275	| **`Badge`** | `40001471:20752` | `State=Primary` (`…20751`) · `State=Hover` (`…20750`) | 33×15 |
276	| **`Stock Status Badge`** | `40001796:7041` | `State=Available` (`…7040`) · `State=Unavailable` (`…7039`) · `State=Low stock` (`…7038`) | 66–79×20 |
277	
278	`Stock Status Badge` appears in **no acceptance criterion**. It maps to `.docs/prd/plp.md` §3
279	("**OUT OF STOCK** shown on tile when all sizes are at or below buffer threshold" and the low-stock
280	indicator) — so the PRD requirement that had no design **does** have one. Its `Low stock` state
281	corresponds to nothing in any AC, and `plp.md` §3 places low-stock *at size level*, not on the tile.
282	
283	### Decomposition correction — three slots move from Content to Media
284	
285	Reading `Image Group / Size=Large` (`40002742:46322`, 288×432) and `Size=Small` (`40002742:46321`,
286	179×268) shows the overlays live on the **image**, not in the text block:
287	
288	| Slot | Frame | Structure | Desktop | Mobile |
289	|---|---|---|---|---|
290	| **`Tag`** (the badge) | 78×48 @ top-left | `touchContainer` 30×24 @ (24,12) → `Label` text 30×8 | ✅ | ✅ |
291	| **`Close`** (remove 'x') | 48×48 @ top-right | `touchContainer` 24×24 → `Icon` 16×16 | ✅ | ✅ |
292	| **`Carousel`** (arrows) | 288×24 @ y=204 (vertically centred) | two `touchContainer` 24×24 @ x=12 and x=252 | ✅ | **absent** |
293	| **`Slide-indicator`** | 179×1, flush to the image's bottom edge (y=267 of 268) | instance | **absent** | ✅ |
294	
295	**Consequences:**
296	
297	1. **The badge slot moves from Step 5 to Step 4.** It is `Tag`, overlaid top-left on the image — not a part
298	   of `Card-content`. Remove the `badge` part from `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`; add a `tag` part to
299	   `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`.
300	2. **The remove ('x') CTA moves from Step 5 to Step 4.** It is `Close`, top-right on the image. The plan had
301	   it in `ZimmProductCardContent` — wrong molecule. Remove `onRemove` handling from Content; it belongs in
302	   Media. The union still carries `onRemove` on the wishlist member; the organism passes it to Media.
303	3. **This makes the split cleaner, not messier:** everything overlaid on the image is Media, everything below
304	   it is Content.
305	4. **§4a and §4b are confirmed by the design itself,** not just by the verbal decision — `Size=Large` has
306	   `Carousel` and no indicator; `Size=Small` has `Slide-indicator` and no `Carousel`.
307	5. **The slide indicator is a 1px hairline flush to the image's bottom edge**, not floating dots. Step 1's
308	   recipe must not assume dot geometry.
309	
310	### Two new findings that need raising, not resolving in code
311	
312	- **🟡 The badge looks interactive, against a requirement that says it must not be.** `Tag` wraps its label in
313	  a **`touchContainer`** — this file's convention for an interactive hit area (the bag icon and both arrows use
314	  the identical wrapper) — and the `Badge` component ships a **`State=Hover`**. But SPR-16 reads
315	  "~~clickable~~ product badges" and `.docs/prd/plp.md:70` says clickable badges are *"a NEW unsigned request —
316	  not confirmed… **Do not implement**."* Two independent signals in Figma versus an explicit written

75	/**

1	/**
2	 * Guard: a multipart recipe's declared `parts` must cover every part the component actually
3	 * reads off `useMultiStyleConfig`.
4	 *
5	 * The failure this catches is silent, though not by the mechanism it looks like: `parts` does
6	 * not gate `baseStyle`. Probed directly against `ChakraProvider`, a recipe declaring
7	 * `parts: ['declared']` while carrying both parts in `baseStyle` and in a variant resolves to
8	 * `{declared: {...base, ...variant}, undeclared: {...base}}` — the undeclared part keeps its
9	 * full base styling and loses only the variant's. `parts` gates `variants`/`sizes`. The base
10	 * SFCC `theme/components/project/header.js` is that same shape shipping in production: 9
11	 * declared `parts` against 13 `baseStyle` keys, and the four it omits (`accountIcon`,
12	 * `arrowDown`, `signoutIcon`, `signoutText`) are each read, spread and styled by
13	 * `components/header/index.jsx` (lines 232, 255, 321, 323) today.
14	 *
15	 * So an undeclared part goes wrong in one of two ways, both quiet. If `baseStyle` covers it, it
16	 * renders correctly and then stops responding to variants and sizes — latent on a recipe with no
17	 * variants today, surfacing only the day someone adds one. If `baseStyle` does not, the read is
18	 * `undefined`, `__css={undefined}` is a legal prop, and the element inherits. Neither is reported
19	 * by `tsc`, eslint, an axe run, or a `play` that only asserts text. The first case is precisely
20	 * the "would survive a refactor invisibly if broken" case .claude/rules/testing.md says to cover,
21	 * so the corrected mechanism strengthens this guard's justification rather than weakening it.
22	 *
23	 * Comparing `parts` against the recipe's own `baseStyle` keys would not catch it: renaming a
24	 * part in both places at once keeps them consistent with each other and still breaks the
25	 * component. The component's reads are the only source of truth for what it needs, so this
26	 * walks the component source.
27	 *
28	 * Scope: `overrides/app/components/**` — every co-located `<name>.css.ts`, which since the
29	 * footer decomposition is where a component's recipe normally lives.
30	 *
31	 * It is not a whole-repo guard, and nothing else covers the remainder: the model is strictly
32	 * sibling-based (a recipe's `parts` are reconciled against the `index.tsx` beside it), so a
33	 * recipe that does not sit next to its component is out of reach. `theme/components/header.ts`
34	 * is the only multipart recipe in that position today and is therefore unguarded.
35	 * `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` does not pick it up either — that suite has no
36	 * parts-vs-reads check of any kind; it guards bare token keys and recipe namespacing.
37	 *
38	 * `READ_RE` recognises only the identifier `styles`, so a second binding in the same component
39	 * is invisible here: `zimmSubscribeModal/index.tsx` reads `chrome.actions`. That one is
40	 * deliberately out of scope rather than a gap to close — `chrome` holds *ZimmModal's* recipe,
41	 * so the sibling model would misattribute `actions` to `zimmSubscribeModal.css.ts`, which
42	 * correctly does not declare it.
43	 */
44	import { describe, expect, test } from 'vitest';
45	import { existsSync, readFileSync, readdirSync } from 'node:fs';
46	import path from 'node:path';
47	
48	const COMPONENTS = path.resolve(process.cwd(), 'overrides/app/components');
49	
50	const walk = (dir: string): string[] =>
51	  readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true }).flatMap((entry) => {
52	    const full = path.join(dir, entry.name);
53	    return entry.isDirectory() ? walk(full) : [full];
54	  });
55	
56	/** `parts: ['root', 'label']` — the literal array in a `.css.ts` recipe. */
57	const PARTS_RE = /\bparts:\s*\[([^\]]*)\]/;
58	/** `styles.label` and `styles['label']`, the two ways a component reads a resolved part. */
59	const READ_RE = /\bstyles(?:\.([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*)|\[\s*'([^']+)'\s*\])/g;
60	
61	/**
62	 * Strips `//` line comments before either regex runs. Without this, a `parts` array with
63	 * inline/trailing comments (header.css.ts's `// Zimmermann additions:` and `// x → migrated to
64	 * y` entries) corrupts the comma split, and a commented-out `styles.foo` reference in a

66	 * requires preserving that dead code, so the scanner has to see past it instead.
67	 */
68	const stripLineComments = (source: string): string => source.replace(/\/\/[^\n]*/g, '');

73	  componentFile: string;

content.text:
# Phase-2 Whole-Feature Re-Audit — SFCC-236 Product Card Shared Component

Branch `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component`, HEAD `3814db6`, 23 commits vs `origin/develop`. No sub-agent dispatch tool was available to me in this session, so I ran every angle myself, sequentially, treating each as an independent pass — including active mutation-testing rather than reading claims at face value.

Working tree confirmed clean before and after (`git status --short` empty throughout); every mutation I introduced for falsification was reverted and verified byte-identical to HEAD via `git diff --exit-code` before moving to the next.

---

## Angle 1 — Compiles and passes

`npx tsc --noEmit` → clean, zero output.

`npm run test -- --run` → **54 files / 873 tests passed**, including `zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx` (56), `zimmProductCardMedia/index.test.tsx` (30), `zimmProductCardContent/index.test.tsx` (27), `recipeGuards.test.ts` (6), `recipeParts.test.ts` (29). All stderr noise ("Could not parse CSS stylesheet") traced to unrelated pre-existing files (list-menu/drawer-menu/header), none from this feature.

`npm run lint` → **FAILS: 8 errors, 18 warnings.** Ran twice for determinism; identical both times.

🔴 **must-fix, CONFIRMED, UNIFORM** — Three of the eight lint errors are brand-new Prettier violations inside this feature's own files, not pre-existing:
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup/index.stories.tsx:54:10`
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.stories.tsx:114:103` ("Insert `,`")
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/nodeCoverage/index.stories.tsx:105:103` ("Insert `,`")

I confirmed via `git diff origin/develop...HEAD --stat` that all three files are wholly new to this branch, and via `git diff` on the other 5 files that they are genuinely untouched by this branch (matching the "5 pre-existing errors/18 warnings" baseline every prior round reported). The last two errors are the *exact same* missing-trailing-comma spot inside the two byte-identical `LiveSizeSelectionCard` copies — confirming this is one authored mistake, duplicated by the accepted duplication, not two independent ones.

This directly contradicts postbuild.md Rounds 2–4's repeated claim "lint 5/18, identical count and identical file set to the pre-fix baseline." Checking the round history: Round 4 was the last round to actually re-run and report lint. Rounds 5, 6, and 7 — which is exactly when `zimmSizeChipGroup/index.stories.tsx` and the two `LiveSizeSelectionCard` copies were authored/modified (the "make every size-chip story interactive" and "un-extract productCardFixtures.ts" commits) — report `tsc`/`test`/`audit:tokens` only, never lint. Lint silently drifted for three rounds while every write-up kept asserting it was clean. This is exactly the kind of thing plan.md's own Step 7 gate and "Baseline pass criteria for every step" (`lint` clean) are supposed to catch, and it directly violates AC-equivalent language in the plan itself. Not CI-gated today (confirmed: `grep lint .github/workflows/qa.yml` → no match), so it won't block a merge mechanically, but it is a real, present, reproducible failure of a command the plan calls "non-negotiable."

---

## Angle 2 — Tokens

`node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` → 1 unacknowledged finding, `overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts:20` (`'59.125em'`) — pre-existing, outside this diff, confirmed via `git diff origin/develop...HEAD -- .../footer.css.ts` (empty). Zero new findings from this feature. `zimmSizeChipGroup.css.ts:40`'s `65px` carries a compliant `audit-allow` comment and appears correctly in the "acknowledged exception" list.

**Semantic intent check** — walked every `var(--zimm-color-*)` in all six new recipe files against its CSS property:
- `color:` → `text.*`/`link.*` (7 instances: `zimmSizeChipGroup.css.ts:43`, `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts:146`, `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts:144,166,172,204`) — all correct category.
- `borderColor:` → `border.*` (`zimmSizeChip.css.ts:93`) — correct category.
- `background:` → `bg.*` (`zimmSlideIndicator.css.ts:56`, active branch) — correct category.
- `background:` → `border.secondary` (`zimmSlideIndicator.css.ts:56`, inactive branch) — genuine mismatch.

This last one, plus `zimmSizeChip.css.ts`'s `border.focus`-reused-for-"selected", are exactly the two items the task named as already-decided-to-ship-as-is (Round 6, Marcel: *"good to ship, the official tokens will just have to follow"*). **Confirmed still accurately described, not re-raising.** No new semantic mismatches found anywhere else in the six recipes.

---

## Angle 3 — Styling conformance

Bare Chakra token keys as JSX props: zero found across every new `index.tsx` (direct grep for `color=`/`bg=`/`padding=`/etc. against scale-shaped literals). `sx=` prop: unused anywhere in this feature. Recipe namespacing/registration: all six recipes registered append-only in `theme/components/index.ts` (diff-verified, pure addition, nothing else touched).

🟡 **should-fix, CONFIRMED, UNIFORM** — **Recipe state exhaustiveness documentation gap.** `zimmSizeChip.css.ts` explicitly cites Figma node IDs and states "*Hover and Active/pressed are NOT part of that variant set*" for its one interactive part. None of the other five new interactive parts across this feature's other two recipe files carry an equivalent statement:
- `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`: `bagButton`, `nameLink`, `notifyMeButton` (all `cursor:pointer`/`onClick`) — the file's only relevant comment (line 18-22) states "no Figma spec exists for **focus**," which is a different claim (about the ring's own sourcing) than "no Figma spec exists for hover/active."
- `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`: `close`, `arrowButton` — no hover/active-related comment at all near either part.

I grepped the whole feature for "Hover/active", "Hover and Active", "NOT part of" and found only the one `zimmSizeChip.css.ts` hit. Plan.md's own Step 5 pass criterion explicitly asked for exactly this comment on the bag button ("*Hover/active: no Figma spec → no rule, commented*") — it isn't there. I have no Figma MCP access, so I cannot verify whether Hover/Active states genuinely don't exist in Figma for these five controls (plausible, given the consistent pattern elsewhere in this design system) — only that the required disclosure is missing. Per this angle's own rule ("If no Figma node exists for a state, say so explicitly rather than leaving it unverified"), this is exactly that unverified state, left unverified in the shipped code.

🔴 **must-fix (gate-level), CONFIRMED via reproducible mutation, UNIFORM** — **`recipeGuards.test.ts`'s exhaustive prop-combination walk never reaches a custom-named boolean recipe prop.** The guard's `DEFAULT_STYLE_PROPS`/`PROP_COMBINATIONS` mechanism only varies five fixed keys (`inverse`, `disabled`, `hasError`, `focused`, `filled`). Three of this feature's six new recipes use custom boolean prop names outside that set: `ZimmSizeChip`'s `selected`, `ZimmSlideIndicator`'s `isActive`, and `ZimmProductCard`'s six flags (`hoverHidesPrice`, `hoverRevealsPrice`, `hoverRevealsSizeSelector`, `hoverRevealsNotifyMe`, `sizeSelectorUnavailable`, `hideBagOnMobile`).

I proved this directly, not by inspection: I introduced a textbook bare-Chakra-colour-key violation (`'text.default'` on `borderColor`) into `zimmSizeChip.css.ts`'s `selected: true` branch — `recipeGuards.test.ts` passed all 6 tests clean. As a control, I put the *identical* mutation into the adjacent `disabled` branch (which *is* varied) — it was caught immediately (`ZimmSizeChip.chip.borderColor: 'text.default'`). Both mutations were reverted and the file confirmed byte-identical to HEAD afterward. This means for `ZimmProductCard`'s recipe specifically, *every* hover-reveal/mobile-hide conditional block (the entire hover-reveal mechanism this component's whole design is built around) is invisible to this "hard gate" — a bare-token mistake anywhere inside those six conditional spreads would ship silently. No live bug exists today (I confirmed every value in the unexercised branches is a correctly-formed `var(--zimm-*)` reference), but the gate itself has a real hole, and this is the first feature to open it in three places at once. `recipeGuards.test.ts` is Tier 2 (UI-designer gated) and untouched by this branch (confirmed via diff) — fixing it is out of SFCC-236's own remit, but it needs raising, per this angle's own instruction that "a designed state with no recipe entry is a finding — it will not be caught by any gate" (here: a *branch*, not just a state, with no gate coverage).

---

## Angle 4 — Structure

Named export matches folder name: confirmed for all six (`ZimmSlideIndicator`, `ZimmSizeChip`, `ZimmSizeChipGroup`, `ZimmProductCardMedia`, `ZimmProductCardContent`, `ZimmProductCard`), each with both the named export and a default export, matching the exemplar (`ZimmColourSwatch`/`ZimmColourSwatchGroup`) exactly. Story present for all six. Test file present for all six. No data-fetching hook in any leaf (grepped every new `index.tsx` for `use[A-Z]`, only `useMultiStyleConfig`/`useState`/`useEffect`/`useRef`/`useIntl` found — `useIntl` is the explicitly-permitted exception).

🟡 **should-fix, CONFIRMED, UNIFORM** — **Props type export is inconsistent across the six new components.** `components.md`'s naming convention is followed by all six (`<Component>Props`), but whether that type is actually *exported* diverges:
- `ZimmSizeChipProps` (atom) — exported via bottom `export type {}`, matching the exemplar's exact pattern.
- `ZimmProductCardMediaProps`, `ZimmProductCardContentProps` — exported directly at declaration.
- `ZimmSlideIndicatorProps`, `ZimmSizeChipGroupProps` — **never exported**, in any form, in either file.

Confirmed via full-repo grep that nothing currently needs either unexported type externally (no functional breakage today), but this is a real, silent deviation from a convention 4 of 6 sibling files in the same feature follow, with no comment explaining why these two don't.

---

## Angle 5 — Imports

No base-path (`@salesforce/retail-react-app`) imports anywhere in this feature (grep-confirmed empty). No relative-import chain deeper than 3 (`../../../icons` is the deepest, exactly at the limit). No cross-import between the two sibling molecules (`zimmProductCardMedia` and `zimmProductCardContent` each import only their own dependencies plus the shared module; neither imports the other). No circular imports. Zero `ZimmSizeSelector` references anywhere in the diff or on disk — the §4d naming-collision rename is completely and verifiably applied, not just claimed.

Clean. Nothing to report on this angle.

---

## Angle 6 — Accessibility

Every `<chakra.img>` (all 3, all in `zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx`) receives a non-empty `alt` sourced from the required (non-optional) `alt: string` field on `ZimmProductCardMediaImage` — enforced at the type level, not just by convention. No `IconButton` used anywhere in this feature (all icon-bearing controls are raw `chakra.button` with an explicit `aria-label` on the button itself: bag, notify-me has visible text so no `aria-label` needed, close, both arrows). Every `onClick` in this feature is attached to a native `<button>`/`chakra.button` — none on a `div`/`span`/`Box` — so the role/tabIndex/onKeyDown requirement for non-native interactive elements doesn't apply anywhere in this feature.

Clean.

---

## Angle 7 — Against the ticket

Cross-checked plan.md's own Step 1–6 pass criteria directly against the shipped code (not against postbuild.md's summary of them):
- Step 1: clamp behaviour, `count<=1` guard, `role="group"`+label (not `aria-hidden`), parts/registration — all confirmed in code.
- Step 2: 4 states present and distinguishable, hover/active explicitly absent+commented, hit area 28px ≥ 24px, recipe keys correctly named — confirmed. (Minor, non-defect observation: the plan's stated Step 2 test-wrapper criterion, "wrap in IntlProvider + MemoryRouter, mock the icons barrel," is boilerplate that doesn't literally apply — neither `ZimmSizeChip` nor `ZimmSizeChipGroup` calls `useIntl`, renders a `Link`, or renders an icon, and their test files correctly use no wrapper at all. Not a finding, just noting the plan text is generic here.)
- Step 3: byte-diff confirmed additive-only, both branches, both loading states, matching the plan exactly.
- Step 4: no `288px`/`179px` literal anywhere in production code (grep-confirmed), primary image always renders, lazy/decoding correct, arrows/indicator mutual exclusion mechanically asserted.
- Step 5: attributes absent from DOM (not hidden) for plp/home, notify-me co-requirement, one heading, explicit media queries (imports `breakpoints` directly, no array shorthand).
- Step 6: two genuine `@ts-expect-error` cases — I independently confirmed both are load-bearing (not decorative) via the fact that `tsc --noEmit` passes clean: an *unfired* `@ts-expect-error` directive is itself a TS error ("Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive"), so a clean compile is a self-verifying proof both are real. Zero `switch`/`if` on `props.variation` (grep-confirmed literally, not just via the docblock's own claimed grep). Exactly one `<a>` per card asserted (`getAllByRole('link')`).

All of Step 6's Fix-C/D/E/F/G mobile/hover logic in `zimmProductCard.css.ts` and `index.tsx` is internally consistent and traces correctly through `VARIATION_CONFIG`.

---

## Angle 8 — Intra-step DRY

Checked specifically for the drift question raised in the task: whether the two independent copies of the `LiveSizeSelectionCard` demo wrapper (`zimmProductCard/index.stories.tsx` vs `nodeCoverage/index.stories.tsx`) have drifted from each other, or from what `zimmProductCardShared.ts` expects.

**No drift found.** Byte-for-byte `diff` (not eyeballing) confirms the `LiveSizeSelectionCard` function body, its full docblock, and the `PRIMARY_IMAGE`/`HOVER_IMAGE`/`SIZES` fixtures are identical between the two files today. Neither file references `CARD_SLOT`/`HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` directly (they only pass props through to `<ZimmProductCard>`), so there's no drift-from-shared-module risk to find there either.

🔵 **note, CONFIRMED, UNIFORM** — While checking this I found the duplication is actually wider than "two copies": the identical 4-entry `[xs,s,m,l]` `SIZES` array and `PRIMARY_IMAGE`/`HOVER_IMAGE` fixtures are typed **four times**, byte-identically, across `zimmProductCardMedia/index.stories.tsx`, `zimmProductCardContent/index.stories.tsx` (SIZES only), `zimmProductCard/index.stories.tsx`, and `zimmProductCard/nodeCoverage/index.stories.tsx`. This is squarely the shape this angle's own rule names ("typed three times with no shared source is a UNIFORM finding even when all three currently agree"). I'm reporting it factually per that rule, but **not** relitigating it as a fresh defect: this is the exact, explicit, deliberate call Marcel made in Round 7 (*"duplicating a demo image or a size array across story files is normal and low-stakes, not a drift risk... should never have been extracted as a shared file"*), reached specifically by un-extracting `productCardFixtures.ts` and articulated as principle, not oversight. Confirmed still true today, still holding, no drift.

---

## Angle 9 — React logic correctness (stateful components)

I mutation-tested three separate pieces of stateful logic rather than trusting the docblocks' claims about them — each time introducing a real regression, confirming the test suite catches it, then reverting and re-confirming the file matches HEAD:

1. **`ZimmSizeChipGroup`'s prop-resync `useEffect`** (`index.tsx:74-76`) — the exact "prop that seeds state on mount receives a different value on re-render" case this angle asks for a fixture for. Broke the dependency array to `[]`; both of the "roving tabindex resync on rerender" tests failed exactly as expected. Restored, confirmed clean.
2. **`ZimmProductCardMedia`'s clamp-on-shrink `useEffect`** (`index.tsx:175-177`) — uses the correct functional-updater form (`setCurrentIndex((index) => Math.min(index, totalSlides - 1))`, reading the *fresh* value the updater receives, not a stale closure over `currentIndex`). Removed the clamp body entirely; the "Fix 3 regression" test (navigate to last of 3, shrink to 2, click next, must wrap on *that* click) failed exactly as its own name promises. Restored, confirmed clean.
3. **`ZimmProductCard`'s hover-structural recipe assertion** (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`, the `:focus-within` price-reveal rule for Home) — removed it; exactly one test (`FOCUS_WITHIN_PRICE_KEY`) failed. Restored, confirmed clean.

All three are genuine, load-bearing tests, not decorative ones that happen to pass. No stale-closure or derived-vs-raw-state defect found in any of the three. `goToRelativeSlide` reads raw `currentIndex` (not a functional updater) but this is safe here — it's a fresh closure per render, invoked only from a user click, with no risk of two updates racing within one render cycle.

---

## Visual checkpoint brief

I have no Figma MCP access this session. The table below is built from the Figma node IDs already cited in the shipped code/plan.md, not from live verification — every row is a DevTools check to run against those cited nodes, and I've flagged where the citation itself couldn't be corroborated (only checked for internal consistency, not fetched).

---

## What I tried to falsify

- **Ran `tsc`/`test`/`audit:tokens` myself** rather than quoting postbuild.md's numbers — all three reproduced. Then **ran `lint`, which no round had checked since Round 4**, and it broke on exactly the files the un-checked rounds touched. This is the one place a prior "clean" claim didn't survive independent re-verification.
- **Mutation-tested three separate pieces of stateful/structural logic** (`ZimmSizeChipGroup`'s resync effect, `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s clamp effect, one of `ZimmProductCard`'s hover-structural assertions) by breaking each and confirming the exact expected test failed, then restoring and confirming clean — not just reading the tests and trusting the docblock's claim that they'd catch a regression.
- **Attacked `recipeGuards.test.ts` directly** — the task calls it "the hard styling gate," so I tried to make it fail on a real violation. It didn't, on the first attempt in the right branch; it did on a control attempt in a branch the guard is known to vary. This is the strongest finding in this report precisely because I disproved the gate's own claimed coverage rather than accepting it.
- **Diffed the two duplicated story-wrapper copies byte-for-byte** rather than eyeballing them, specifically because the task asked whether the recent un-extraction had let them drift. It hadn't — confirmed, not assumed.
- **Grepped for the specific fabricated-citation failure mode** (already caught and fixed twice earlier in this build) across every remaining file, and found a third, still-live instance at `zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx:38` that Round 4 had flagged but that was never fixed or explicitly deferred by Marcel — it's absent from the task's own "known, deliberately-deferred" list, so I'm reporting it here for the first time as still open: the comment claims `overrideStyling.md` "confirms" no link override exists, but I read `overrideStyling.md` directly (line 182) and it says the opposite (asserts `link/index.tsx` "already" exists as a bridge-pattern example) — verified independently that `overrides/app/components/link/` genuinely doesn't exist on disk, so the underlying *fact* is true, only the *citation* is backwards. 🟡 should-fix, CONFIRMED, UNIFORM (fourth occurrence of this exact failure shape in one build).
- **Checked every `var(--zimm-color-*)` in the six new recipes against its CSS property by hand**, not just trusted the two already-flagged exceptions were the only ones.

## What I could not verify

- **No live Figma access this session** (no MCP tools available) — every Figma-node claim in this report is a citation-consistency check (code vs. plan.md, code vs. itself), not a live corroboration. This is the same limitation prior rounds recorded; I did not close it.
- **`zimmProductCardMedia/index.test.tsx` and `zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx`'s remaining ~80 assertions** were not each individually mutation-tested — I spot-checked one representative structural assertion per file (the clamp effect, the focus-within reveal) and confirmed both are real; I did not re-derive the other ~80% of assertions in these two large files by hand, so a decorative assertion elsewhere in them is possible but unconfirmed either way.
- **Whether Figma genuinely has no Hover/Active state for `close`/`arrowButton`/`bagButton`/`nameLink`/`notifyMeButton`** (Angle 3 finding) — I confirmed the required disclosure comment is absent; I cannot confirm whether that's because the omission is correct (no such state exists) or because it was missed, without Figma access.
- **CodeRabbit review** — Step 7 (Gate and PR) is explicitly not yet reached per the plan and postbuild.md, and I found nothing to contradict that (no PR exists, confirmed no local uncommitted state). Not evaluated, correctly out of scope for this round.
- I did **not** re-verify the items the task explicitly told me were closed decisions not to re-raise (the two token-category gaps, the manifest-citation files, the three wishlist CRM items, the Sep 21 design-lock date, `globalStyles.ts`'s CODEOWNERS gap) — I spot-confirmed each is still accurately described where doing so was nearly free (token gaps, manifest files), and left the rest untouched per the instruction.

---
